example:
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status` does not warn. After a
third such commit, no version in the window names it, and `habeas status` warns
about `parse`. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
rationale:
The referenced test covers the scenario and both warning outcomes of `requirements.references.coverage.reauthored`.

- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[project]` creates a Git repository containing an unreferenced `parse` function and no coverage-window override. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[record]` writes evidence inputs obtained by reading the selected outline items; the test initially records `fn[parse]` for the checking requirement (named `rules.check` in this fixture).
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]` commits that evidence, then rewrites and commits it twice with empty input lists and distinct rationales. After each commit it asserts that only `helper` is warned about, so `parse` remains covered through the second reauthoring with the default window.
- The same test commits a third rewrite with no inputs and asserts that the warnings now contain `parse` as well as `helper`. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[warned]` obtains these names from the actual coverage-warning API.
- The status-report integration is also exercised by `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete]`: it asserts that status omits the warning for covered `parse` and includes it when the available evidence history no longer covers it. This complements the precise three-reauthoring assertions without requiring reassessment of the cited history and reporting requirements.

The mandatory inputs include a `{test}` reference to the example, and no gap was found.
